rv.q: CADEL: Lungs on Legs reminds us how brilliant Fringe theatre can be as Connor Delves takes us on an exhilarating journey through the highs and lows of a professional cyclist's career.

But beyond this, the characterization of Evans is a bit anodyne. We see some self-doubt creeping in as he fails to succeed, and there are hints that he may have a bit of a temper, but these are brushed off fairly quickly. Delves gives us a slightly camp, rather bland figure which doesn’t seem to do justice to the real Cadel Evans.
It is informative, entertaining, charming and inspirational.
This Tour de France tale is a triumphant Tour de Force.
This is pitch-perfect theatre-making that manages to be utterly clear, technically brilliant and emotionally compelling all at the same time.
